dedupe_keys.name: thermally passive low income housing demonstration in bhuj gujarat india with hunnarshala foundation

description: This case study tests passive cooling for low-income housing in Bhuj, Gujarat, India, where heatwaves are deadly: in May 2015 an estimated 2,500 people in India died in heatwaves above 46 degrees Celsius. It is reported in a 2017 master's thesis by Emma Nelson in MIT's Department of Mechanical Engineering, carried out with the Hunnarshala Foundation, a non-governmental organisation based in Bhuj. The work combined prototype field work, simulations and the construction of pilot homes to bring thermally passive techniques into affordable housing, and gives recommendations on roof design, wall design and fan use. With an appropriate design, measured operative temperatures in the pilot homes met the ASHRAE 80 per cent acceptability criteria for more than 60 per cent of operating hours and stayed within the Indian IMAC 80 per cent range for 88 per cent of hours in Bhuj's climate. Coverage: pilot homes in Bhuj. Access: the thesis is openly available from MIT's DSpace repository. Licence: MIT thesis terms; free to read. Caveats: a small number of pilot homes in one hot-dry climate. Simulation uses: evidence for heat-adaptation measures in housing models and for building guidelines under India's Housing for All programme. Related records: the EDCS courtyard energy dataset and CAHDC design conditions.
